title: Bitcoin Slips Ahead Of Fed Week, Big Tech Earnings: Analysts Divided On Where BTC Is Headed Next
summary: Analyst Michaël van de Poppe pointed to BTC’s 120% annualized return since 2011 against 6% for gold.
content:
Bitcoin slipped below $80,000 on Monday, dipping to around $79,330 in the past day, near its lowest level since mid-September.

Analyst Ted Pillows warned that losing the $80,000 zone on the weekly chart could lead to "capitulation soon."

The Fed decides on rates Wednesday, with Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon earnings also set to be released this week.

Bitcoin's (BTC) price slipped below $80,000 on Monday ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision and earnings from Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOG), and Amazon (AMZN) this week, with crypto analysts split on where Bitcoin is headed next.

The Fed will announce its rate decision on Wednesday. Traders are pricing a 90.6% chance that it holds rates at 3.75% to 4%, and a 9.4% chance of a hike to 4% to 4.25%, according to CME FedWatch. Investors will also watch for any signs of a hike in December.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Microsoft and Alphabet are set to report earnings on Wednesday, followed by Amazon on Thursday. Meta (META) increased its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to $135 billion-$145 billion, and SpaceX (SPCX) expected $35 billion-$40 billion in fourth-quarter CapEx.

Heavy spending in AI could propel investors to find growth opportunities and could divert capital into tech stocks and away from Bitcoin. But if worries about AI returns spark a wider selloff, Bitcoin could drop as investors de-risk. In contrast, a tech rebound could boost risk appetite and help BTC.

Michael Van de Poppe, founder of MN Fund, explained that Bitcoin's long-term record made the current dip a buying opportunity. "Bitcoin's return is annualized 120% since 2011," he wrote on X, compared with 6% for gold.

He said investors should "bet big" on Bitcoin when it was undervalued against gold, and suggested rotating that money back into gold "in 1-2 years, when Gold is done with its correction." According to Poppe, Bitcoin was down 7.3% in 2026, and gold was down 7.5%.

However, not every analyst shared that view. Ted Pillows said in a post on X that Bitcoin "looks like it wants to go lower," adding that any rally was "just because of shorts closing rather than spot demand." He warned that if Bitcoin lost the $80,000 zone on the weekly chart, "we could see capitulation soon."

His comments came as Bitcoin's price traded around $79,930, down 0.8% over the past 24 hours and falling over 3% in the last week. The apex cryptocurrency was trading at around its lowest level since mid-September. The slide followed a combined $773 million in outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs last week, as per SoSoValue data.

On-chain analysts James Check and Michael Sullivan took up a similar question and asked whether Bitcoin was in "the fabled disbelief rally…or just another bear market rally."

title: Bitcoin On Track To Post Weakest October In Six Years As US Buyers Retreat Ahead Of Fed Decision
summary: Inflation risks could complicate the outlook for Bitcoin, with crude oil above $100 a barrel since early October, the Federal Reserve's rate decision, and the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections as potential macro factors.
content:
Bitcoin traded around $80,800 on Wednesday, down over 4% in October, putting the cryptocurrency on track for its weakest October in six years.

Bitcoin spot demand has also remained negative since Oct. 14, while short-term holders' profit buffer narrowed.

CryptoQuant's Bull Score Index fell from 90 to 60, meaning that a bullish phase remains but is currently cooling.

Bitcoin (BTC) is bracing for its weakest October in six years as U.S. investors retreat from the market ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision later on Wednesday.

The cryptocurrency traded around $80,800 on Wednesday morning. It was down 4.2% for the month. Bitcoin closed September at $83,567 and fell to $80,051 by Oct. 28. That's up from an average October gain of 18.1% since 2020. Bitcoin also lost 3.8% in October 2025. Another drop will make it the weakest October in six years.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Coinbase Premium has not had a positive day this October, CryptoQuant said in a post on X Tuesday. The index measures the price difference between Bitcoin on Coinbase and offshore exchanges. A negative reading means U.S. buyers are paying less than buyers abroad, a sign of soft demand.

The premium dropped to -0.146 on Oct. 24, the lowest since June 30, the firm said in a report on Tuesday. Its October average of -0.093 is three times that of September. Spot demand overall has also been negative every day since Oct. 14, the report said. New buyers are taking in coins slower than miners are creating them.

CryptoQuant said short-term traders have lost most of the buffer. Bitcoin traded 8.1% above the realized price on Oct. 26. That metric measures the average price of coins that have been held between one and three months, and stands at $74,041. The gap was 33.4% on Sept. 22.

CryptoQuant's Bull Score Index, which aggregates 10 market indicators, has fallen from 90 to 60. The firm said that still indicates a bullish but cooling phase. A reading of 50 or less would mean a regime change. CryptoQuant has set support between $73,000 and $77,600. According to the on-chain firm, the Fed decision and the Nov. 3 midterms are the two tests ahead that are to decide the apex currency's next move.

The macro backdrop offers little respite. Energy-driven inflation could keep policy tight longer, as markets expect the Fed to hold rates, Bitunix analysts said. One analyst cited a Reuters survey in which economists raised inflation forecasts for 31 of 50 economies for 2027. Crude oil has been above $100 a barrel since early October, analysts said. The firm added that a hawkish signal from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh could force bullish bond bets to unwind.

Bitcoin's price was trading around $81,400, up over 1% in the last 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment remained in the 'bearish' zone, accompanied by 'normal' chatter levels over the past day.

title: Crypto Market Today, Oct. 28: Bitcoin and Altcoins Gain as Fed Decision Clears the Way for Big Tech Earnings
summary: Bitcoin extended its recovery above $81,000 as the Fed held interest rates steady, with investors now turning their attention to major Big Tech earnings that could shape the market's next move.
content:
As of early evening on Oct. 28, Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) rose 0.52% to $81,220.35, Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) rose 0.68% to $2,363.24, and Solana (CRYPTO:SOL) rose 1.33% to $102.60.

Bitcoin and the broader cryptocurrency market posted back-to-back gains despite a busy week of economic developments.

Most notably, the Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rate steady at 3.75% to 4%, in line with market expectations. However, the central bank acknowledged that inflation remains elevated, leaving the possibility of future rate hikes on the table.

Investors will now turn their attention to a wave of corporate earnings. Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) , and ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) are scheduled to report after Wednesday's market close. Any disappointing results, particularly from these major technology companies, could weigh on broader market sentiment and put pressure on crypto's recent gains.

Fortunately, Spot crypto ETFs traded firmer over the last few days. The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (NASDAQ:IBIT) up 0.96%, Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (NYSEMKT:FBTC) up 1.01%, and iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (NASDAQ:ETHA) up 1.07%.

The next development to watch is whether these price gains translate into renewed investor demand. A return to sustained ETF inflows would provide a more convincing sign that the market is stabilizing.

With the Federal Reserve's decision in the rearview, attention now shifts toward corporate earnings and what they reveal about the broader economy.

This week's reports from major technology companies should provide valuable insight into consumer and business spending, corporate profitability, and the AI infrastructure boom that has helped drive much of the market's recent growth. Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) and Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) are slated to report Thursday after the closing bell.

For crypto investors, the next move may depend as much on these broader market developments as on events within the digital asset industry itself.

Encouragingly, several major cryptocurrencies remain above their summer lows despite the recent correction. However, the recovery is far from convincing, and disappointing earnings or renewed inflation concerns could quickly put sellers back in control.

title: Bitcoin little-changed at $80.4k as oil, rate jitters dent crypto appetite
summary: Investing.com-- Bitcoin moved slightly lower on Monday after logging sharp losses over the weekend, as persistent concerns over rising oil prices and anticipation of key central bank meetings largely dented appetite for cryptocurrencies.
content:
Investing.com-- Bitcoin moved slightly lower on Monday after logging sharp losses over the weekend, as persistent concerns over rising oil prices and anticipation of key central bank meetings largely dented appetite for cryptocurrencies.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The world's largest crypto edged down 0.3% to $80,425.7 by 11:01 ET (09:01 GMT).

Bitcoin slid by about $2,000 over the weekend as sentiment showed little improvement amid a sustained decline in global technology stocks, and as markets positioned for more hawkish signals from the world's biggest central banks in the coming days.

Bitcoin was trading close to the bottom end of an $80,000 to $87,000 trading range established over the past month, amid a dearth of positive cues for crypto markets.

While oil prices slid from six-month highs on Monday– following a report of more talks between Middle Eastern powers and Iran– they still remained close to annual peaks, leaving markets on edge over their impact on the global economy.

Adding to the risk aversion, a host of major central banks are set to meet this week, with the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank, and the Bank of Japan widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

But all three banks are expected to present a hawkish outlook in the face of increasingly sticky inflation and energy risks, leaving the door open for more rate hikes later in the year.

Higher rates bode poorly for risky, speculative assets like crypto, and stand to further pressure prices in the long term.

Tracking Bitcoin, broader crypto prices also rose marginally Monday.

A seasonal trend of crypto price strength in October– dubbed as "uptober"-- failed to materialize for a second consecutive year, as retail and institutional sentiment towards the sector remained weak.

World no.2 crypto Ether slid 0.7% to $2,327.05, while XRP added 0.2%.

Solana added 0.6%, Cardano rose 0.5%, while BNB gained 0.4%.

Among memecoins, Dogecoin rose 0.7% and $TRUMP climbed 2.8%.

Vahid Karaahmetovic contributed to this report.

As of early evening on Oct. 26, the broader cryptocurrency market extended its losing streak amid fading risk appetite. Notably, Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) fell 0.28% to $79,817.06, Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) fell 0.58% to $2,313.61, and Solana (CRYPTO:SOL) fell 0.94% to $100.30.

The recent selling across crypto markets appears to be driven by two main factors.

First, traders are reducing their exposure ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Oct. 28. Investors often become more cautious leading up to major economic announcements, particularly when the outcome could influence interest rates and broader market sentiment.

Second, the crypto market is coming off a strong finish to the third quarter, with several cryptocurrencies posting double-digit rebounds from their summer lows. Some profit-taking after a rally of that magnitude is hardly surprising, particularly as investors weigh the potential impact of the Fed's upcoming decision.

When looking at crypto ETF's, they experienced a similar wave of selling. The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (NASDAQ:IBIT) fell 1.61%, Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (NYSEMKT:FBTC) fell 1.66%, and iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (NASDAQ:ETHA) fell 3.22%.

Continued weakness in crypto markets heading into Wednesday's Federal Reserve meeting remains a likely possibility as investors take a cautious approach. Although the market is pricing in just an 8% probability of a rate hike, uncertainty surrounding the Fed's decision and subsequent commentary could keep volatility elevated.

For crypto to regain its footing in the near term, investors should watch whether Bitcoin can defend the $80,000 zone and whether major altcoins begin showing signs of renewed strength. Stabilization across these assets could signal improving risk appetite, while further declines would suggest sellers remain in control.

Moreover, corporate Bitcoin buying has slowed. For instance, Strategy ( NASDAQ:MSTR ), which holds 848,517 BTC, added no Bitcoin in the week leading up to October 25. Its last purchase, revealed on October 12, was only 250 BTC—a small amount for the market's largest corporate buyer.

Bitcoin has also mirrored tech stocks in 2026, raising concerns that a sell-off in AI-focused stocks could drag its price down further. Markets are also awaiting the Federal Reserve's rate decision on October 28. If the support level around $80,000 breaks, the next significant level to watch will be the True Market Mean at $77,600.

Whether this is a good time to buy Bitcoin largely depends on your investment strategy and how you would react to potential price drops. Long-term investors might view $80,000 as a noteworthy price point. However, due to ETF outflows and slowing corporate purchases, Bitcoin may test the $77,600 level first.

A lump-sum investment might work well if Bitcoin rallies immediately, while dollar-cost averaging—investing fixed amounts at scheduled intervals—could help minimize losses if the price drops initially.

A price recovery would likely happen in stages. First, Bitcoin would need to hold above its recent 30-day low of $79,107, then break back above $81,500 and its 50-day average of $81,802, all while ETF inflows turn positive.

content:
Investing.com -- Bitcoin was slightly higher on Tuesday, helped by a surge in risk sentiment and a fall in oil prices. The two factors slightly outweighed caution a day ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and a pause in purchases of the world's largest cryptocurrency by top corporate holder Strategy.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Bitcoin was last up 1.3% to $81,119.3 by 17:42 ET (21:42 GMT), recovering after briefly dropping to $79,496.8 earlier. The crypto thus fell below an $80,000 to $87,000 trading range established over the past month.

A risk-on mood dominated proceedings on Tuesday, with equities rising as the artificial intelligence trade surged for a second straight session on enthusiasm around Anthropic's long-awaited initial public offering filing.

A decline in oil prices also helped sentiment. Brent crude futures settled 1.5% lower at $114.07 a barrel, after ongoing diplomatic efforts between regional Middle Eastern powers offset supply disruption fears. Iran on Monday held a quadrilateral meeting of itself, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Türkiye.

Crypto market participants were also gearing up for the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) policy decision on Wednesday. The FOMC is broadly expected to leave rates unchanged, after having hiked rates in September for the first time since 2023.

The odds of no action from the FOMC have been reinforced despite hotter-than-expected U.S. consumer and producer inflation reports earlier this month, following Fed Chair Kevin Warsh recently declining to provide any guidance on the decision.

Elsewhere, Strategy made no bitcoin purchases or sales and sold no shares under its at-the-market program during the week of October 19 to 25, 2026.

As of October 25, it holds about 848,517 bitcoin, bought for a total of $64.02 billion at an average of roughly $75,446 per coin, including fees and expenses.

During the week, the company repurchased 2,068,459 shares of its STRC preferred stock (Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Stretch Preferred) for $204.9 million, paid from USD cash reserves. It bought back no other security class.

Strategy did not disclose why it had purchased no new Bitcoin. But a pause in its buying offered some negative cues to markets, especially after the company sold some of its Bitcoin holdings earlier this year.

Despite recent underwhelming price performance, Galaxy said it remains confident in Bitcoin's long-term prospects and that now is the time to accumulate.

"We think the bear market ended in June and that bitcoin is in the accumulation phase that has preceded every prior advance," Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy, said in a note titled "Why now is the time to add and hold BTC."

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Thorn said the bear market likely ended in June with prices under $58,000, and that improving chart signals, reduced selling pressure and mounting fiscal risks make the largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization attractive to accumulate.

He pointed to bitcoin's recovery above its 50-week moving average after 44 weeks below it. Five consecutive weekly closes above that level have strengthened his conviction that a bottom is in.

The selloff highlights Bitcoin's vulnerability to shifting macroeconomic conditions, as rising oil prices, geopolitical uncertainty and concerns over stretched technology valuations undermine investor appetite for risk. With the Federal Reserve's policy decision approaching, traders are watching whether tightening liquidity and persistent inflation could trigger further losses across digital assets.

Bitcoin fell 5.4% after reaching $84,800 early last week, recording five consecutive daily declines and briefly breaking below $80,000 to hit a weekend low of $79,200. Hilbert Senior Portfolio Manager Jesse Marre identified the $75,500 level as a critical threshold, warning that a break below it could undermine the bullish market base built since the summer lows.

The weakness in cryptocurrencies coincided with a broader retreat in risk assets. Renewed tensions involving Iran pushed Brent crude oil prices towards $117 a barrel amid speculation about a possible US military offensive. However, oil prices retreated after US President Donald Trump said no immediate offensive was planned, although prices remained elevated.

Technology shares also came under pressure as investors reassessed valuations in the artificial intelligence sector. Nvidia shares fell 8% over the week, while Meta Platforms dropped 9%. The Nasdaq Composite lost about 2%, following an intraw eek decline of roughly 3.6%, while the S&P 500 fell 1%, according to Hilbert's October 26 market update.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Bitcoin is now testing technical support between $78,500 and $79,500. A recovery above $81,400 could help restore near-term stability, while moves above $85,000 and $87,500 would be needed to strengthen the outlook for another rally. A sustained breakout above $87,500 could open the way towards $95,000-$98,000, Marre said.

Tightening liquidity is adding to the pressure on digital assets. Hilbert's global liquidity index stood at 3.06, while its six-factor model recorded a weekly decline of 0.47 in its Z-score, indicating deteriorating liquidity momentum.

Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded net inflows of $442 million over the week despite $635 million in outflows on Thursday alone. The pattern suggested that fund flows largely followed movements in the spot market rather than driving prices, according to the report.

Attention now turns to the US Federal Reserve's policy decision on Wednesday, with markets pricing in an 87% probability that the central bank will leave interest rates unchanged. Marre expects a hawkish hold, with policymakers likely to keep the possibility of a December rate increase open amid persistent inflation and resilient economic growth.

Investors will also assess US personal consumption expenditures inflation and gross domestic product data due on Thursday, followed by the Chicago purchasing managers index on Friday. The releases could influence expectations for monetary policy and determine whether pressure on risk assets persists.

title: $8 Trillion in Big Tech Earnings, Fed Decision and Inflation Data: Bitcoin's Next Big Test?
summary: The Federal Reserve's Oct. 28 decision, followed by US inflation and GDP figures, could reshape expectations for interest rates and Bitcoin. Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon…
content:
Key Takeaways

The Federal Reserve's Oct. 28 decision, followed by US inflation and GDP figures, could reshape expectations for interest rates and Bitcoin.

Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon report earnings as investors question whether massive AI infrastructure spending can deliver sustainable returns.

Bitcoin's recent weakness near $80,000 puts the spotlight on interest rates, institutional demand and whether crypto can withstand another technology-stock selloff.

Bitcoin faces a critical test during the week of Oct. 26, as major central bank decisions, US inflation data, and earnings from technology giants converge over the course of the week.

The Federal Reserve is expected to announce its interest rate decision Wednesday, followed by third-quarter US GDP and September personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation figures Thursday.

Meanwhile, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon will report quarterly earnings, putting the artificial intelligence investment boom under scrutiny.

The timing is particularly important for cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin recently slipped toward $79,100 after struggling to maintain the $80,000 level, while concerns about inflation and technology valuations have weakened investor confidence.

The Federal Reserve's Oct. 28 announcement is arguably the week's most important scheduled event for Bitcoin.

Following September's rate increase, the federal funds target range stands at 3.75% to 4.00%. Markets largely expect policymakers to hold rates unchanged .

According to CME FedWatch probabilities reported by MarketWatch on Oct. 26, traders assigned approximately a 9% probability to another quarter-point increase this week, rising to 73% for December.

That makes the Fed's forward guidance potentially more influential than Wednesday's decision itself.

Higher interest rates increase the appeal of interest-bearing assets while raising borrowing costs and tightening financial conditions. Bitcoin, which generates no contractual yield, can face pressure when investors demand greater compensation for holding riskier assets.

Coinbase Institutional's Oct. 16 research supports this connection. It found Bitcoin had shown greater resilience than semiconductor stocks during recent AI-related selloffs but remained sensitive to changes in interest rate expectations.

The report identified the $80,000 to $82,000 region as important near-term support, with further downside potentially bringing the $72,000 to $74,500 area into focus.

Wednesday brings earnings from Alphabet and Microsoft, followed by Amazon on Thursday.

Alphabet and Microsoft represent roughly $8 trillion in market value, making their results particularly important for the technology sector.

Investors will examine Microsoft's Azure cloud growth, Alphabet's advertising and cloud businesses, and Amazon's AWS performance. But the bigger question concerns the returns generated by billions of dollars committed to AI infrastructure.

Reuters reported that disappointing results from Meta and Lam Research had already weakened technology stocks, raising concerns about whether AI spending can sustain elevated valuations.

The earnings calendar adds another dimension: approximately 542 companies valued above $2 billion are scheduled to report this week, with Wednesday and Thursday accounting for 73% of the market capitalization represented.

Strong results could restore confidence in growth-sensitive assets, including cryptocurrencies. However, disappointing cloud growth or higher-than-expected capital expenditures could intensify selling pressure.

Bitcoin's reaction is not guaranteed to mirror the Nasdaq. Coinbase's research suggests its correlation with semiconductor stocks has weakened, indicating that monetary policy may currently matter more than AI-related equity movements.

Thursday's economic releases introduce another potential source of volatility.

According to Morningstar's economic calendar, September headline PCE inflation is forecast at 3.6% annually, compared with 3.4% in August. Core PCE is expected at 3.1%, up from 3.0%.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis has scheduled both PCE and third-quarter GDP figures for Oct. 29 at 8:30 a.m. ET.

Higher-than-expected inflation could reinforce expectations of another Fed rate hike in December. Conversely, softer inflation could reduce pressure on Treasury yields and support risk assets.

GDP presents a more complicated picture. Strong growth may indicate economic resilience, but combined with persistent inflation, it could also justify keeping monetary policy restrictive.

International developments add another risk.

The Bank of Japan concludes its policy meeting Friday, Oct. 30, with its benchmark rate currently around 1.25%.

A surprise hawkish signal could strengthen the yen and encourage investors to unwind yen-funded carry trades, potentially reducing liquidity across global financial markets.

For Bitcoin , the central question is whether institutional demand can absorb another macroeconomic shock.

A combination of softer inflation, reassuring Fed guidance, and stronger technology earnings could support a recovery. However, persistent inflation, hawkish central banks, and disappointing AI results could deepen the selloff.

With several major announcements arriving within 48 hours, Bitcoin investors face a test of whether the cryptocurrency can maintain its footing as global financial conditions shift.
